subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Should gateway security owners close this report as non-reproducible under the current authenticated WebSocket trust model, or request a PoC demonstrating acceptance of an unauthenticated or cross-device frame?
rationale: The alleged sequence-based authorization mechanism does not exist in current source, but the protected security label requires an explicit owner decision before closure.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that event sequence values are non-secret ordering metadata and close unless a boundary-crossing PoC is provided.

options.title: Request exploit proof
options.body: Keep the report pending while asking for an attacker model and reproducible frame-injection or authentication-bypass transcript.

options.title: Commission protocol audit
options.body: Perform a broader review of transport integrity, replay handling, authentication, and device authorization independently of this sequence-ID claim.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence values are non-secret ordering metadata and close unless a boundary-crossing PoC is provided.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history connects this contributor directly to gateway authentication, pairing, and remote-client hardening in the affected connection handler.
